kinematics.consistency_check: the mean of the piecewise profile over the antrum is 3.88 mm/s against an independently published antral average of 5.9 mm/s - a DISAGREEMENT of -34%. The profile was built only from the corpus value and the terminal-antral acceleration, so this is an independent check and it does not pass.  The likely cause is geometric: this subject's antrum measures 72.5 mm along the centreline against a published antral length of 30-40 mm, so the slow proximal portion dominates the average, whereas in a 35 mm antrum almost the whole length would lie inside the accelerating terminal 28 mm.  The profile was NOT retuned to hit 5.9 mm/s.
kinematics.why_that_number_matters: a global scale pulse would displace EVERY ring at t=0.  Most rings being undisplaced is what distinguishes a travelling wave from a breathing balloon, and the browser re-measures this count on the live geometry rather than trusting this file.

micro_scale.statement: the gland column is drawn at 60x and the mucus gel at 480x in the nested inset.  Both factors are shown in the HUD; nothing in the micro view is at organ scale and the page never implies it is.

declared_gains.note: no time or speed gain is applied to the motility animation: at 3 cycles/min a wave crosses the antrum in 39 s, which is watchable in real time.  The only declared magnifications are SPATIAL, in the micro view.
